    # Per-column statistics (observable outputs, match original code).
    mean[j]: out DATA_TYPE = j          # mean of column j
    stddev[j]: out DATA_TYPE = j        # standard deviation of column j

    # Memory overhead is O(M), negligible compared to N*M and M*M,

parameters:

    M: int                 # number of columns
    float_n: DATA_TYPE     # N as DATA_TYPE, as in the original kernel
    eps: DATA_TYPE         # small positive threshold, = 0.1 in PolyBench

computation:
    # 0. Precompute constants used many times.
    sqrt_n = sqrt(float_n)
    inv_sqrt_n = 1.0 / sqrt_n

    # 1. Column means:
    #    mean[j] = (1/N) * sum_i data[i,j]
    for j:
        mean[j] = (1.0 / float_n) * sum(i, data[i, j])

    # 2. Column standard deviations, using the same two-pass formula as the
    #    original code, including the clamp for near-zero values:
    #
    #    var_j   = (1/N) * sum_i (data[i,j] - mean[j])^2
    #    std_raw = sqrt(var_j)
    #    stddev[j] = (std_raw <= eps) ? 1.0 : std_raw
    #
    # This is exactly the semantics of sqrt_exo + clamp_stddev.
    for j:
        var_j = (1.0 / float_n) * sum(i, (data[i, j] - mean[j]) * (data[i, j] - mean[j]))
        std_raw = sqrt(var_j)
        stddev[j] = (std_raw <= eps) ? 1.0 : std_raw

    # 3. Per-column normalization scale.
    #    We keep stddev[j] itself intact (as in the original code) and
    #    compute an auxiliary scale[j] used during normalization:
    #
    #        scale[j] = 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[j])
    #
    #    so that normalization can be done via a multiply instead of a divide
    #    in the inner loops.
    for j:
        scale[j] = inv_sqrt_n / stddev[j]

    # 4. Normalize data in place:
    #
    #    Original Exo code:
    #        data[i,j] = data[i,j] - mean[j]
    #        data[i,j] = data[i,j] / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[j])
    #
    #    Here we use scale[j] to avoid repeated sqrt/divisions:
    #        data[i,j] = (data[i,j] - mean[j]) * scale[j]
    #
    #    This keeps the final normalized data[i,j] identical up to
    #    floating-point re-association.
    for i, j:
        data[i, j] = (data[i, j] - mean[j]) * scale[j]

    # 5. Correlation matrix as Gram matrix of normalized columns:
    #
    #    The original code computes, for i < j:
    #        corr[i,i] = 1.0
    #        corr[i,j] = sum_k data[k,i] * data[k,j]
    #        corr[j,i] = corr[i,j]
    #    and sets corr[m-1,m-1] = 1.0.
    #
    #    This is equivalent to:
    #        corr[p,q] = sum_k data[k,p] * data[k,q]
    #    for all p,q, plus an explicit unit diagonal.
    #
    #    We use the symmetric Gram-matrix formulation here, which matches
    #    the original result but is more amenable to blocking and GEMM-like
    #    optimizations.
    for p, q:
        corr[p, q] = sum(k, data[k, p] * data[k, q])

    # 6. Enforce exact unit diagonal (same as original PolyBench kernel).
    for j:
        corr[j, j] = 1.0

optimization:
    # General notes:
    # - All transformations preserve the mathematical result up to standard
    #   floating-point reordering differences that also arise from tiling.
    # - Extra memory is limited to the O(M) "scale" vector.

    # 1) Hoist invariant scalar work.
    #    sqrt_n and inv_sqrt_n are computed once, outside all data-dependent
    #    loops. scale[j] is computed once per column and reused N times.
    #    (This is reflected directly in the computation section.)

    # 2) Exploit independence across columns for mean and stddev.
    #
    #    For fixed j, the reductions over i for mean[j] and stddev[j] are
    #    independent for different j. We parallelize across j so each thread
    #    owns one or more columns, maximizing cache reuse over the i loop.
    parallelize(j)          # applied to the loops computing mean[j] and stddev[j]

    # 3) Normalize data with row-major traversal and SIMD over columns.
    #
    #    data is row-major (i * M + j), so we normalize with i as the outer
    #    loop and j as the inner loop. This makes data[i,*] contiguous and
    #    amenable to vectorization.
    parallelize(i)          # distribute rows across cores
    vectorize(j, VF)        # VF tuned to SIMD width (e.g., 4/8/16 lanes)

    # 4) Optimize correlation as a symmetric blocked GEMM:
    #       corr = data^T * data
    #
    #    Dimensions:
    #       - output indices: p, q in [0, M)
    #       - reduction index: k in [0, N)
    #
    #    We tile p, q, and k to improve cache locality and to expose a
    #    small "micro-kernel" that can aggressively use registers and SIMD.
    block(p, P, TP)         # TP ~ 32–64: tile size for first column index
    block(q, Q, TQ)         # TQ ~ 32–64: tile size for second column index
    block(k, K, TK)         # TK ~ 64–256: tile size over rows (reduction)

    hoist(P)                # make P (p tile) the outermost loop
    hoist(Q)                # nest Q just inside P
    hoist(K)                # place K outside the inner micro-kernel loops

    parallelize(P)          # distribute independent (P,Q) tiles across cores

    # Within each (P,Q,K) tile, use an outer-product style micro-kernel:
    #
    #   for each K-tile:
    #     for each p in P-tile:
    #       tmp_p = data[K, p]                   # scalar reused across Q-tile
    #       for each q in Q-tile:
    #         corr[p, q] += tmp_p * data[K, q]   # contiguous over q, good for SIMD
    #
    # This matches the mathematical definition corr[p,q] += sum_k data[k,p]*data[k,q].
    vectorize(q, VF) within tiles   # SIMD across the innermost q loop
    unroll(k, UK) within tiles      # small unroll factor UK to reduce loop overhead

    # 5) Optional symmetry exploitation (pure optimization, same result):
    #
    #    Since corr is symmetric, we can optionally avoid computing both
    #    (p,q) and (q,p) by:
    #      - Restricting tiles to q >= p, and
    #      - After each tile, copying corr[p,q] into corr[q,p].
    #
    #    This roughly halves the arithmetic cost for large M while keeping
    #    the final corr identical (up to FP reorder effects).
    #    The model keeps this as an explicit comment rather than a hard
    #    requirement, as it complicates tiling but not semantics.

domain:
    i: dim in [0, n)        # observation index (rows of data)
    j: dim in [0, m)        # feature index (columns of data, and indices into mean/stddev)
    p: dim in [0, m)        # row index of correlation matrix
    q: dim in [0, m)        # column index of correlation matrix

data:
    data[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * m + j
        # N x M input data matrix, row-major.
        # On input: raw samples.
        # On output: centered and normalized samples (used to form correlation).

    corr[p, q]: out DATA_TYPE = (p, q) -> p * m + q
        # M x M correlation matrix, row-major, symmetric.

    mean[j]: out DATA_TYPE = j -> j
        # Column means; written by the kernel (driver does not read them).

    stddev[j]: out DATA_TYPE = j -> j
        # Column standard deviations after clamping (matching PolyBench semantics).

    inv_scale[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = j -> j
        # Temporary: 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[j]) used to normalize columns.
        # Adds only O(m) extra memory, well within the 50% overhead constraint.

    eps: temp DATA_TYPE
        # Numerical threshold used to clamp near-zero standard deviations.

    sqrt_n: temp DATA_TYPE
        # Precomputed sqrt(float_n) to avoid redundant square roots.

parameters:
    n: size                  # number of observations (rows)
    m: size                  # number of variables/features (columns)
    float_n: DATA_TYPE       # equals n cast to DATA_TYPE; provided by driver.


computation:
    #-----------------------------------------------
    # 0. Constants / precomputations
    #-----------------------------------------------
    eps = 0.1                    # Matches SCALAR_VAL(0.1) / original PolyBench code.
    sqrt_n = sqrt(float_n)       # One SQRT instead of per-element SQRT in the original kernel.

    #-----------------------------------------------
    # 1. Column means:
    #      mean[j] = (1/n) * sum_i data[i,j]
    #
    # Implementation streams through data row-major (i outer, j inner),
    # improving cache locality vs. column-wise sweeps.
    #-----------------------------------------------
    for j in [0, m):
        mean[j] = 0.0
    for i in seq(0, n):          # sequential over rows
        for j in [0, m):
            mean[j] += data[i, j]
    for j in [0, m):
        mean[j] = mean[j] / float_n

    #-----------------------------------------------
    # 2. Center data and accumulate column variances in a single pass.
    #
    # After this phase:
    #   - data[i,j] holds (data_orig[i,j] - mean[j])   (centered in-place),
    #   - stddev[j] holds sum_i (data[i,j])^2          (sum of squared deviations).
    #
    # This fuses the original “stddev” and “centering” loops, computing
    # (data - mean) only once per element while retaining exact math.
    #-----------------------------------------------
    for j in [0, m):
        stddev[j] = 0.0
    for i in seq(0, n):          # stream rows for row-major locality
        for j in [0, m):
            data[i, j] = data[i, j] - mean[j]
            stddev[j] += data[i, j] * data[i, j]

    #-----------------------------------------------
    # 3. Finalize stddev and clamp near-zero values.
    #
    #   stddev[j] = sqrt( (1/n) * sum_i (data_orig[i,j] - mean[j])^2 )
    #   if stddev[j] <= eps: stddev[j] = 1.0
    #
    # This matches the original PolyBench correlation kernel, which uses
    # sqrt then a value-dependent clamp (implemented via clamp_stddev extern).
    #-----------------------------------------------
    for j in [0, m):
        stddev[j] = stddev[j] / float_n
        stddev[j] = sqrt(stddev[j])
        if stddev[j] <= eps:
            stddev[j] = 1.0

    #-----------------------------------------------
    # 4. Precompute per-column scaling factors:
    #
    #     inv_scale[j] = 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[j])
    #
    # This replaces:
    #   - one SQRT per data element, and
    #   - one DIV per data element,
    # with:
    #   - one global SQRT, and
    #   - one DIV per column.
    #-----------------------------------------------
    for j in [0, m):
        inv_scale[j] = 1.0 / (sqrt_n * stddev[j])

    #-----------------------------------------------
    # 5. Scale centered data so each column has unit variance:
    #
    #    data[i,j] := data[i,j] * inv_scale[j]
    #
    # After this, for non-clamped columns, sum_i data[i,j]^2 ≈ 1.
    # This is algebraically equivalent to:
    #   (data_orig[i,j] - mean[j]) / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[j])
    # from the Exo kernel.
    #-----------------------------------------------
    for i in seq(0, n):
        for j in [0, m):
            data[i, j] = data[i, j] * inv_scale[j]

    #-----------------------------------------------
    # 6. Compute symmetric m x m correlation matrix.
    #
    # For normalized data (columns with unit variance),
    # correlation is the Gram matrix of columns:
    #
    #   corr[p,q] = sum_i data[i,p] * data[i,q]   for p != q
    #   corr[p,p] = 1.0                           (set explicitly)
    #
    # The original kernel:
    #   - sets corr[p,p] = 1.0 explicitly, and
    #   - fills only the upper triangle via a reduction over rows,
    #     then mirrors it to the lower triangle.
    # We preserve that behavior but express the reduction directly.
    #-----------------------------------------------
    # Strictly upper triangle via reductions over observations.
    for p in [0, m):
        for q in [p + 1, m):
            corr[p, q] = sum(i, data[i, p] * data[i, q])

    # Symmetrize: copy upper triangle into lower triangle.
    for p in [0, m):
        for q in [p + 1, m):
            corr[q, p] = corr[p, q]

    # Set the diagonal to exactly 1.0, matching the reference implementation
    # (and masking any small normalization / clamping drift).
    for p in [0, m):
        corr[p, p] = 1.0


optimization:
    #------------------------------------------------
    # Tuning parameters (positive integers):
    #   TJ_data   – tile size for feature dimension when streaming data.
    #   VJ_data   – SIMD width for feature-wise operations.
    #   TP_corr   – tile size for corr row (p) dimension.
    #   TQ_corr   – tile size for corr column (q) dimension.
    #   TI_corr   – tile size for observation (i) reduction in correlation.
    #   UI_corr   – unroll factor for reduction over i within a tile.
    #   VQ_corr   – SIMD width when accumulating corr over q.
    #
    # These are chosen based on cache sizes and vector width on the
    # target x64 CPU (e.g., 32–64 for L1 / AVX2, larger for L2 / AVX-512).
    #------------------------------------------------

    # 1. Phases that stream through data[i,j] (means, centering+variance, scaling)
    #    already use i as the outer loop and j as inner, which is optimal for
    #    row-major layout. We tile and vectorize j to improve cache and SIMD use.
    block(j, Jm, TJ_data)          # j = Jm * TJ_data + j_inner; tile feature dimension.
    hoist(Jm)                      # Make the tile loop over Jm outermost where applicable.
    vectorize(j, VJ_data)          # Vectorize inner feature loop within a tile.

    # 2. Correlation as a blocked Gram matrix:
    #      corr[p,q] = sum_i data[i,p] * data[i,q]
    #
    # We block both feature dimensions (p, q) and the reduction over i.
    block(p, P, TP_corr)           # Tile corr rows.
    block(q, Q, TQ_corr)           # Tile corr columns.
    block(i, Icorr, TI_corr)       # Tile observations in the reduction dimension.

    # Hoist P and Q so that we work on one corr tile (P,Q) at a time,
    # accumulating over Icorr tiles of observations. This:
    #   - keeps each corr tile in L1/L2,
    #   - streams rows of data only once per tile, and
    #   - improves temporal locality for corr updates.
    hoist(P)
    hoist(Q)

    # 3. Parallelism:
    #    Different (P,Q) tiles of corr are independent reductions over i.
    #    We parallelize the outer tile loop over P (and optionally Q)
    #    to exploit multi-core CPUs.
    parallelize(P)                 # Distribute corr-row tiles across threads.
    # Optionally enable 2D parallelism over tiles (runtime permitting):
    # parallelize(Q)

    # 4. Micro-optimizations inside tiles:
    #    - Unroll the reduction over i within a tile to reduce loop overhead
    #      and enable more aggressive instruction scheduling.
    #    - Vectorize across q within a (P, Icorr) stripe to exploit SIMD loads
    #      from data[i, *] and contiguous corr[p, *].
    unroll(i, UI_corr)             # Unroll the inner reduction over observations within Icorr.
    vectorize(q, VQ_corr)          # Vectorize along q inside each corr tile row.

    # Summary of optimization effects:
    #   - Fewer passes over data and fewer (expensive) sqrt/div operations.
    #   - Row-major streaming for all data[i,j] traversals.
    #   - Blocked, cache-resident correlation tiles (Gram matrix-style).
    #   - Exposed SIMD parallelism along feature dimensions.
    #   - Exposed thread-level parallelism across corr tiles.

domain:
    # Problem sizes (PolyBench: N samples, M variables)
    i: dim in [0, N)           # row / observation index
    j: dim in [0, M)           # column / variable index
    p: dim in [0, M)           # first correlation index
    q: dim in [0, M)           # second correlation index
    k: dim in [0, N)           # row index used for correlation accumulation

data:
    # All arrays are stored row-major as in the C/Exo code
    data[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * M + j
        # Initially: raw input data
        # After kernel: centered and scaled data used to form the correlation

    corr[p, q]: out DATA_TYPE = (p, q) -> p * M + q
        # Symmetric M×M correlation matrix

    mean[j]: out DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
        # Column means

    stddev[j]: out DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
        # Column-wise standard deviations after clamping

    x_row[j]: scratch DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
        # Temporary buffer of length M holding one normalized row of data
        # Used only during correlation accumulation; extra memory is O(M),
        # well below the 50% overhead constraint.

parameters:
    float_n: DATA_TYPE   # equals N, but passed as DATA_TYPE in PolyBench
    eps: DATA_TYPE       # small positive value, 0.1 in the reference code

    # Tunable blocking / vectorization parameters (chosen for target CPU/cache):
    TI_mean: int         # tile size over i when accumulating statistics
    TJ_stats: int        # tile size over j for mean/stddev/normalization
    TP_corr: int         # tile size for first correlation index p
    TQ_corr: int         # tile size for second correlation index q
    VEC_J: int           # vector length for operations along contiguous j/q

computation:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Compute column means: mean[j] = (1/n) * sum_i data[i,j]
    #    Reordered to traverse data row-major (i outer, j inner).
    #------------------------------------------------------------

    # 1a. Initialize means
    for j in [0, M):
        mean[j] = 0.0

    # 1b. Accumulate sums row by row (row-major access of data)
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, M):
            mean[j] += data[i, j]

    # 1c. Divide by float_n to get means
    for j in [0, M):
        mean[j] = mean[j] / float_n

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Compute column standard deviations (with clamping).
    #
    # stddev[j]_acc = sum_i (data[i,j] - mean[j])^2
    # variance[j]   = stddev[j]_acc / float_n
    # s[j]          = sqrt(variance[j])
    # stddev[j]     = 1.0 if s[j] <= eps else s[j]
    #
    # This matches the Exo/PolyBench semantics using sqrt_exo and clamp_stddev.
    # Loop order is again row-major for better cache behavior.
    #------------------------------------------------------------

    # 2a. Zero accumulators
    for j in [0, M):
        stddev[j] = 0.0          # used as accumulator for sum of squares

    # 2b. Accumulate squared deviations row by row
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, M):
            tmp = data[i, j] - mean[j]
            stddev[j] += tmp * tmp

    # 2c. Finalize standard deviations with sqrt and clamping
    for j in [0, M):
        variance_j = stddev[j] / float_n
        s_j = sqrt(variance_j)
        if s_j <= eps:
            stddev[j] = 1.0
        else:
            stddev[j] = s_j

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Center and scale each column in-place.
    #
    # data[i,j] <- (data[i,j] - mean[j]) / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[j])
    #
    # This matches the Exo code, but sqrt(float_n) is hoisted so it is
    # computed only once.
    #------------------------------------------------------------

    sqrt_n = sqrt(float_n)

    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, M):
            data[i, j] = (data[i, j] - mean[j]) / (sqrt_n * stddev[j])

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Compute symmetric correlation matrix corr = data^T * data.
    #
    # After normalization, the correlation is:
    #   corr[p, q] = sum_k data[k,p] * data[k,q]
    #
    # We implement this as a sequence of symmetric rank‑1 outer products:
    #
    #   For each row k:
    #       x_row[j] = data[k,j]          # copy one row contiguously
    #       corr[p,q] += x_row[p]*x_row[q] for all 0 <= p <= q < M
    #
    # This is mathematically equivalent to the original triple loop over
    # (i, j, k), but:
    #   - Global memory accesses to data are now strictly row-major and
    #     each element data[k, j] is loaded exactly once per row.
    #   - corr is updated in upper-triangular form and later mirrored.
    #------------------------------------------------------------

    # 4a. Initialize full correlation matrix to zero
    for p in [0, M):
        for q in [0, M):
            corr[p, q] = 0.0

    # 4b. Accumulate outer products for each normalized row
    for k in [0, N):
        # Copy the k-th row into a contiguous scratch buffer once
        for j in [0, M):
            x_row[j] = data[k, j]

        # Symmetric rank‑1 update on upper triangle
        for p in [0, M):
            for q in [p, M):
                corr[p, q] += x_row[p] * x_row[q]

    # 4c. Enforce symmetry and set diagonal to 1.0 as in the original
    for p in [0, M):
        corr[p, p] = 1.0
        for q in [p + 1, M):
            corr[q, p] = corr[p, q]

dependencies:
    # Statistical phases must occur in order:
    #   mean -> stddev -> normalization -> correlation.
    #
    # Mean must complete before stddev uses it:
    for j in [0, M):
        MEAN_FINAL(j) -> STDDEV_ACCUM(*, j)

    # Stddev must complete before normalization uses it:
    for j in [0, M):
        STDDEV_FINAL(j) -> NORM_DATA(*, j)

    # Normalization must complete before correlation reads data:
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, M):
        NORM_DATA(i, j) -> CORR_ACCUM(*, *, i)


optimization:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # General scalar hoisting and strength reduction
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Precompute constants once:
    #   inv_n  = 1.0 / float_n
    #   sqrt_n = sqrt(float_n)
    # and reuse them in all loops to avoid redundant divisions/square roots.
    # (These are logical transformations; exact syntax depends on backend.)
    #------------------------------------------------------------

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1–3. Statistics and normalization over data
    #------------------------------------------------------------

    # Tile and vectorize along the contiguous column dimension j in all
    # phases (mean, stddev accumulation, normalization). This improves
    # cache reuse and enables SIMD.
    block(j, J_stats, TJ_stats)          # tile columns into chunks of TJ_stats
    hoist(J_stats)                       # outer J_stats loop around i/j work
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)                  # SIMD across contiguous elements

    # For large N (many rows), further tile the i dimension to fit in cache.
    block(i, I_mean, TI_mean)           # i-tile size chosen to fit data tile and
                                        # mean/stddev working sets into L1/L2

    # Columns (j) are independent for both mean and stddev, so we can
    # parallelize across j-tiles in these phases using OpenMP-style
    # parallel loops:
    parallelize(J_stats)                 # each thread updates disjoint ranges
                                        # of mean[j] / stddev[j]

    # Normalization phase reads/writes data[i,j] but has no inter-column
    # dependencies either, so the same tiling and parallelization over J_stats
    # apply there as well.

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Correlation: symmetric rank‑k update
    #------------------------------------------------------------

    # View the correlation as:
    #   corr = sum_k x_k x_k^T
    # where x_k is the normalized row k. This is a sequence of symmetric
    # rank‑1 updates (BLAS SYR), or equivalently a blocked symmetric GEMM.

    # Block along p and q to operate on submatrices of corr that fit in cache.
    block(p, P, TP_corr)                 # tile rows of corr
    block(q, Q, TQ_corr)                 # tile columns of corr

    # Restrict work to upper triangular tiles (Q >= P) to avoid redundant
    # computation, since the lower triangle is filled by copying at the end.

    # For each k, reuse x_row in registers/L1 to update all tiles touching
    # that row:
    #   hoist the k-loop outside of P/Q tiles so that an entire row is
    #   copied once and then reused.
    hoist(k)

    # Within each (P, Q) tile, make the inner loop over q the fastest-varying
    # index to get unit-stride access to corr[p,q] and x_row[q].
    interchange(q, p)                    # inside each tile: q-inner, p-outer
    vectorize(q, VEC_J)                  # SIMD dot-products within a row of corr

    # Tiles of corr are disjoint in (p, q), so we can parallelize across P
    # (and optionally across Q for Q >= P) without races:
    parallelize(P)                       # distribute corr row-blocks across cores
    # (An implementation may use nested or collapsed OpenMP parallel loops
    # over (P, Q) tiles, respecting the triangular structure.)

    # Optional micro-optimizations inside tiles:
    #   - unroll small inner loops over q and p to reduce loop overhead
    #   - use fused multiply-add instructions (FMA) when available
    #   - align x_row and corr blocks to cache-line / SIMD width boundaries
    unroll(q, factor=2)                  # example: small unroll for better ILP

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Memory footprint considerations
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # The only extra buffer is x_row of length M (O(M) space). This keeps the
    # total memory footprint within ~O(N*M + M*M + M), i.e., the overhead is
    # negligible compared to the original arrays and far below the allowed
    # additional 50% of memory usage.

domain:
    t: dim in [0, n)           # observation index (rows of data)
    i: dim in [0, m)           # feature / column index
    j: dim in [0, m)           # second feature / column index for correlation pairs

data:
    # Row-major input data matrix: data[t, i] = original value of feature i for observation t
    data[t, i]: inout DATA_TYPE = (t, i) -> t * m + i

    # Row-major m x m correlation matrix
    # Only upper triangle is accumulated; lower triangle is filled by symmetry at the end.
    corr[i, j]: out DATA_TYPE   = (i, j) -> i * m + j

    # Per-column statistics
    mean[i]:   out DATA_TYPE    = (i)    -> i
    stddev[i]: out DATA_TYPE    = (i)    -> i

    # Temporary per-column scaling factor:
    #   scale[i] = 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[i])
    # Used to eliminate per-element sqrt + division during normalization.
    scale[i]:  scratch DATA_TYPE = (i)   -> i

parameters:
    float_n: DATA_TYPE          # n as DATA_TYPE, passed in from the driver
    eps:     DATA_TYPE          # small positive threshold, set to 0.1 in the driver

    # Tuning parameters (compile-time or runtime constants):
    TI: int                      # tile size for i (columns) in the correlation phase, e.g., 32 or 64
    TJ: int                      # tile size for j (columns) in the correlation phase, e.g., 32 or 64
    TT: int                      # tile size for t (observations) in the correlation phase, e.g., 64 or 128
    Vcorr: int                   # vector width for correlation updates along j
    Vnorm: int                   # vector width for normalization/statistics loops along i
    Ustat: int                   # unroll factor for mean/stddev accumulation along i

computation:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 0. Precompute sqrt_n once (strength reduction for normalization)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let sqrt_n = sqrt(float_n)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Column means: mean[i] = (1/n) * sum_t data[t, i]
    #    Traversal is row-major (t outer, i inner) to get unit-stride
    #    access in 'i' for the row-major data[t, i] layout.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for i:
        mean[i] = 0.0

    for t, i:
        mean[i] += data[t, i]

    for i:
        mean[i] = mean[i] / float_n

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Column standard deviations:
    #    stddev[i] = sqrt( (1/n) * sum_t (data[t, i] - mean[i])^2 )
    #    Then clamp small stddev to 1.0 to match PolyBench behavior:
    #        if stddev[i] <= eps: stddev[i] = 1.0
    #    Traversal again uses row-major order.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for i:
        stddev[i] = 0.0

    for t, i:
        let diff = data[t, i] - mean[i]
        stddev[i] += diff * diff

    for i:
        stddev[i] = sqrt(stddev[i] / float_n)
        # Implements clamp_stddev(stddev[i], eps): x <= eps ? 1.0 : x
        stddev[i] = (stddev[i] <= eps ? 1.0 : stddev[i])

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Precompute per-column scaling factors:
    #       scale[i] = 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[i])
    #    This converts the per-element division in the normalization
    #    phase into a multiply, and hoists sqrt(float_n) out of the loop.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for i:
        scale[i] = 1.0 / (sqrt_n * stddev[i])

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Center and scale each column in-place:
    #       data[t, i] <- (data[t, i] - mean[i]) * scale[i]
    #    This is equivalent to the original:
    #       (data[t, i] - mean[i]) / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[i])
    #    but uses only multiplies in the inner loop.
    #    Layout is row-major: t outer, i inner.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for t, i:
        data[t, i] = (data[t, i] - mean[i]) * scale[i]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Correlation matrix:
    #       corr[i, j] = sum_t data[t, i] * data[t, j],  for i < j
    #       corr[i, i] = 1.0
    #       corr[j, i] = corr[i, j]
    #
    #    We:
    #      - Initialize diagonal to 1.0 and upper triangle to 0.0
    #      - Accumulate the upper triangle with t (rows) outermost to
    #        stream 'data' row-wise once per observation
    #      - Copy the upper triangle to the lower triangle at the end
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    # 5a. Initialize diagonal and upper triangle
    for i:
        corr[i, i] = 1.0
        for j:
            if j > i:
                corr[i, j] = 0.0

    # 5b. Main accumulation: t outermost for good data locality.
    #     Only update entries with j > i (upper triangle).
    for t:
        for i:
            for j:
                if j > i:
                    corr[i, j] += data[t, i] * data[t, j]

    # 5c. Enforce symmetry: corr[j, i] = corr[i, j] for i < j
    for i, j:
        if j > i:
            corr[j, i] = corr[i, j]

optimization:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Loop ordering and strength reduction
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # - All passes over 'data' use row-major order: outer loop on t,
    #   inner loop on i. This gives unit-stride access along i and
    #   reuses each cache line of data[t, :] fully before moving on.
    # - sqrt(float_n) is computed once (sqrt_n) and reused everywhere.
    # - scale[i] hoists 1 / (sqrt_n * stddev[i]) so that normalization
    #   uses a multiply instead of an expensive division.
    hoist(t)        # ensure t is the outer loop in passes over data
    # (Conceptual: hoisting sqrt_n and scale computations out of
    #  normalization is already encoded in the computation.)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Correlation kernel optimizations
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Correlation dominates runtime: O(m^2 * n).
    # We optimize it via blocking, vectorization, and parallelism.

    # 1) Tile the column indices (i, j) so that corr tiles fit well in cache.
    #    Only the upper triangle (j > i) is active inside tiles.
    block(i, I, TI)       # I: tile index over the first column dimension
    block(j, J, TJ)       # J: tile index over the second column dimension

    # 2) Optionally tile over observations to improve temporal locality
    #    when n is large, so that each (I, J) tile is updated for a block
    #    of rows at a time.
    block(t, T, TT)       # T: tile index over the observation dimension

    # After blocking, the correlation accumulation has an effective
    # structure like:
    #   for T:                      # over tiles of rows
    #     for I, J:                 # over tiles of (i, j)
    #       for t in T:
    #         for i in I:
    #           for j in J with j > i:
    #             corr[i, j] += data[t, i] * data[t, j]

    # 3) Parallelize across tiles in the i-dimension.
    #    For a fixed (t, I, J), each (i, j) pair with j > i is written
    #    by exactly one thread, so there are no data races.
    parallelize(I)

    # 4) Vectorize the innermost loop over j for correlation updates.
    #    This uses SIMD to update multiple corr[i, j] values at once
    #    while streaming data[t, j] contiguously.
    vectorize(j, Vcorr)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Mean / stddev / normalization optimizations
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # - These passes are O(n * m) and much cheaper than correlation,
    #   but we still exploit SIMD and simple unrolling.
    # - The inner loops are along i with unit-stride memory access.
    vectorize(i, Vnorm)   # vectorize statistics and normalization over columns
    unroll(i, Ustat)      # unroll small inner loops over i to reduce loop overhead

    # Note:
    # - Additional tiling over t for statistics/normalization is possible
    #   but usually unnecessary since they are bandwidth-light compared
    #   to the correlation kernel.
    # - The temporary array 'scale[m]' is O(m), so total extra memory is
    #   negligible (< 50% overhead) compared to data[n, m] + corr[m, m].

    # Input data matrix: shape [N, M], row‑major
    data[i_obs, j_feat]: inout DATA_TYPE =
        (i_obs, j_feat) -> i_obs * M + j_feat

    # Output correlation matrix: shape [M, M], row‑major
    corr[j_feat, k_feat]: out DATA_TYPE =
        (j_feat, k_feat) -> j_feat * M + k_feat

    # Per‑feature statistics: 1D arrays, contiguous
    mean[j_feat]: inout DATA_TYPE =
        j_feat -> j_feat
    stddev[j_feat]: inout DATA_TYPE =
        j_feat -> j_feat

    # Local temporary used for normalization scale; same length as `stddev`
    #   norm_factor[j] = 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[j])
    norm_factor[j_feat]: local DATA_TYPE =
        j_feat -> j_feat

parameters:
    float_n:  DATA_TYPE  # number of observations, matches N but stored as DATA_TYPE
    eps:      DATA_TYPE  # small threshold for stddev clamping, typically 0.1

    # Tunable performance parameters (chosen per target machine)
    T_N:        int      # tile size along observation dimension N  (e.g., 64–256)
    T_M:        int      # tile size along feature dimension M      (e.g., 32–128)
    VEC_WIDTH:  int      # SIMD vector width (e.g., 4 for f64 AVX2, 8 for f32 AVX2)

computation:
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 0. Scalar precomputations (hoisted completely out of data loops)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    inv_float_n = 1.0 / float_n       # reuse instead of dividing by float_n repeatedly
    sqrt_n      = sqrt(float_n)       # uses PolyBench-appropriate SQRT for DATA_TYPE
    inv_sqrt_n  = 1.0 / sqrt_n

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Column means: mean[j] = (1/float_n) * sum_i data[i,j]
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Mathematically:
    #   mean[j] = inv_float_n * Σ_{i=0..N-1} data[i,j]
    for j_feat:
        mean[j_feat] = inv_float_n * sum(i_obs, data[i_obs, j_feat])

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Column standard deviations with epsilon clamp
    #    stddev[j] = sqrt( (1/float_n) * Σ_i (data[i,j] - mean[j])^2 )
    #    if stddev[j] <= eps: stddev[j] = 1.0
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    for j_feat:
        var_j = inv_float_n * sum(
            i_obs,
            (data[i_obs, j_feat] - mean[j_feat])^2
        )
        stddev[j_feat] = sqrt(var_j)
        if stddev[j_feat] <= eps:
            stddev[j_feat] = 1.0

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Per‑column normalization factor:
    #    norm_factor[j] = 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[j])
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # This moves all divisions by sqrt_n and stddev[j] out of the large
    # i×j normalization loop, so that inner loops use only multiplications.
    for j_feat:
        norm_factor[j_feat] = inv_sqrt_n / stddev[j_feat]

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Center and normalize columns in-place:
    #    data[i,j] ← (data[i,j] - mean[j]) * norm_factor[j]
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # After this step, each feature column has zero mean and unit L2 norm:
    #   Σ_i (data[i,j]^2) = 1, up to floating‑point roundoff.
    for i_obs, j_feat:
        data[i_obs, j_feat] =
            (data[i_obs, j_feat] - mean[j_feat]) * norm_factor[j_feat]

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Correlation matrix from normalized data
    #    correlation(i,j) = Σ_k data[k,i] * data[k,j]
    #    with corr[i,i] = 1.0 and symmetry corr[j,i] = corr[i,j]
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    for j_feat:
        corr[j_feat, j_feat] = 1.0     # exact unit self‑correlation on the diagonal

    for j_feat:
        for k_feat in [j_feat+1, M):    # only upper triangle, j_feat < k_feat
            corr[j_feat, k_feat] =
                sum(i_obs, data[i_obs, j_feat] * data[i_obs, k_feat])
            corr[k_feat, j_feat] = corr[j_feat, k_feat]   # enforce symmetry

optimization:
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # General notes:
    #   - All scalar precomputations (inv_float_n, sqrt_n, inv_sqrt_n) are
    #     hoisted outside array loops by construction in the computation.
    #   - We keep the mathematical definitions unchanged while restructuring
    #     loops for locality, vectorization, and parallelism.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # A. Mean and stddev reductions:
    #    - Independent across j_feat (columns), so we parallelize there.
    #    - Reductions are over i_obs, which we vectorize where possible.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    parallelize(j_feat)              # each thread handles a subset of columns
    vectorize(i_obs, VEC_WIDTH)      # SIMD across the reduction over rows

    # (Conceptually, schedules for these reductions can look like:)
    #   for j_feat in PARALLEL:
    #       mean[j]   = inv_float_n * sum_i data[i,j]      # row-wise reduction
    #       stddev[j] = sqrt(inv_float_n * sum_i (...))    # row-wise reduction
    #   where sum_i is implemented as a vectorized loop over i_obs.

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # B. Centering and scaling (normalization) of data:
    #    - Operates over the full 2D domain (i_obs, j_feat).
    #    - We tile both dimensions to walk `data` row-major in cache blocks.
    #    - Parallelize across row tiles; vectorize across columns.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    block(i_obs, I_norm, T_N)        # tile rows: i_obs  -> (I_norm, i_obs_inner)
    block(j_feat, J_norm, T_M)       # tile cols: j_feat -> (J_norm, j_feat_inner)
    hoist(I_norm)
    hoist(J_norm)
    parallelize(I_norm)              # distribute row tiles across cores
    vectorize(j_feat, VEC_WIDTH)     # contiguous columns are SIMD-friendly

    # Resulting loop shape (conceptually):
    #   for I_norm in parallel:
    #     for J_norm:
    #       for i_inner in [0, T_N):
    #         for j_inner in [0, T_M) vectorized:
    #           data[...] = (data[...] - mean[j]) * norm_factor[j]

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # C. Correlation phase: corr = data^T * data (symmetric rank‑k update)
    #    - Treat as GEMM-style computation with:
    #        output indices: (j_feat, k_feat) over M × M
    #        reduction index: i_obs over N
    #    - Use 3D tiling: Jb (rows of corr), Kb (cols of corr), Ib (observations).
    #    - Exploit symmetry by skipping tiles with Jb > Kb and mirroring results.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    block(j_feat, Jb, T_M)           # corr row tiles
    block(k_feat, Kb, T_M)           # corr col tiles
    block(i_obs, Ib, T_N)            # reduction tiles over observations
    hoist(Jb)
    hoist(Kb)
    hoist(Ib)

    # Only compute tiles where Jb <= Kb (upper triangle),
    # then copy each completed tile to its symmetric partner.
    parallelize(Jb)                  # distribute corr row-tiles across cores
    vectorize(k_feat, VEC_WIDTH)     # SIMD across contiguous corr columns
    unroll(i_obs, 4)                 # unroll the small inner reduction loop for ILP

    # Conceptual inner structure within each upper-triangular tile:
    #
    #   for Jb in PARALLEL:
    #     for Kb in [Jb, ...):
    #       # local tile C_block[Jb..Jb+T_M, Kb..Kb+T_M]
    #       for Ib:
    #         for j_inner in [0, T_M):
    #           for k_inner in [max(0, j_inner when Jb == Kb) .. T_M) vectorized:
    #             # reduction over i_obs within [Ib..Ib+T_N)
    #             corr[Jb+j_inner, Kb+k_inner] +=
    #                 sum(i_inner in [0, T_N)):
    #                     data[Ib+i_inner, Jb+j_inner] *
    #                     data[Ib+i_inner, Kb+k_inner]
    #
    #       # After finishing an (upper) tile:
    #       if Jb != Kb:

    #                corr[Kb..Kb+T_M, Jb..Jb+T_M]

    # This preserves:
    #   corr[j,k] = Σ_i data[i,j] * data[i,k], for j < k,
